# `mount_repower`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Power-cycle the mount through a fixed sequence of GPIO writes with delays.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build and 32-bit build, command-socket invocation) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xc8830 (64-bit build); helper MountRepower (64-bit build). Power-toggle interpretation INFERRED |

No parameters are read. The handler issues GPIO writes in order: selector 11 low then a 100 ms sleep, selector 7 low then a 100 ms sleep, selector 7 high. The reply is sent after the sequence (at least about 200 ms of requested delay plus GPIO latency). INFERRED: this toggles the power of the mount; the selector-to-rail mapping was not audited. There is no parked or mode gate. If a write fails the error code of the GPIO layer is forwarded and earlier writes may already have happened.

Side effects: Drives GPIO lines in a fixed sequence, probably power-cycling the mount electronics (INFERRED); the mount may disconnect or lose position knowledge (INFERRED). Full command-socket calls also incur the shared diagnostic (logging) writes; this is why the strict grade is MUTATOR even for the read-only calls.

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

A failed GPIO write forwards the GPIO layer error code, which is unresolved (no mount_repower-specific code is assigned).

## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":29,"method":"mount_repower"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"mount_repower","result":0,"code":0,"id":29}
```
